If you see an injured stray dog:
1. Keep a safe distance and do not make sudden movements, as pain can cause a frightened dog to snap.
2. Cover the dog gently with a blanket or towel to keep it warm and calm.
3. Do not give oral food or water if the dog is unconscious or in shock.
4. Contact a 24/7 NGO rescue ambulance or veterinary hospital immediately on our Help & Contacts page.

URGENT BITE FIRST AID PROTOCOL:
1. Wash the wound thoroughly under running tap water with soap for at least 15 minutes immediately.
2. Do NOT apply tight bandages, soil, or home remedies on the wound.
3. Visit a hospital or doctor IMMEDIATELY to start Anti-Rabies Vaccination (ARV) and Immunoglobulin (RIG).
4. Rabies is 100% preventable if post-exposure vaccination is started promptly.

Feeding Street Dogs Guidelines:
• Safe foods: Boiled rice with chicken/curd, boiled eggs, dog kibble, chapatis with plain water.
• Avoid: Chocolate, onions, garlic, cooked poultry bones, sugary sweets, and excessive milk (can cause diarrhea).
• Feed at fixed daily times in quiet spots away from heavy traffic or doorways.

Animal Birth Control (ABC) Program in India:
• Under ABC Rules 2023, street dogs are humanely caught, sterilised, vaccinated against Rabies, ear-notched for identification, and released back into their exact original territory.
• Relocating street dogs to other areas is illegal under Indian law.
• Contact your municipal stray dog cell or local ABC partner NGO.

Legal Rights & Animal Laws in India:
• Section 11 of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (PCA) Act 1960 makes beating, starving, or abandoning any animal a criminal offense.
• Citizens have a legal right to feed street dogs protected by High Court guidelines.
• To report animal cruelty, lodge an FIR at your local police station or contact SPCA.

You can find verified 24/7 rescue helplines, veterinary trauma hospitals, and municipal stray dog cells on our Help & Contacts page. We do not display unverified phone numbers in chat to ensure accurate emergency dispatch.

Caring for Stray Puppies:
• Check if the mother dog is nearby before removing puppies.
• Keep puppies warm with towels and hot water bottles wrapped in cloth.
• Feed specialized puppy weaning formula or diluted warm goat milk; avoid cow's milk.
• Seek foster care or shelter assistance via our Help & Contacts directory.

Weather & Seasonal Care for Street Animals:
• Summer: Place clean water bowls in shaded street corners. Symptoms of heatstroke include heavy panting, drooling, and weakness—cool the body with damp towels.
• Monsoon: Provide elevated dry shelter away from waterlogging and check for tick/flea infestations.

EMERGENCY PROTOCOL WHEN ALL CLINICS / HOSPITALS ARE CLOSED:

1. Check 24/7 Trauma Centers First:
   • In Bengaluru, major centers like CUPA Trauma Center (080 2294 7307) and Government Veterinary Hospital at Queen's Road operate 24-hour casualty emergency units.
   • Use our 'Verified Help Directory' tab to filter by '24/7 Helplines'.

2. Vital First-Aid Precautions (Do No Harm):
   • Bleeding / Trauma: Apply continuous, firm direct pressure with clean, sterile cloth or gauze for 10-15 minutes without lifting. Do NOT use tight tourniquets or wire.
   • Shock / Low Body Heat: Keep the dog warm and calm in a quiet, dark room or covered basket with clean blankets. Shock kills faster than injuries.
   • Suspected Poisoning: Do NOT induce vomiting with salt water or oil (causes aspiration pneumonia). Give activated charcoal paste or electrolyte water if fully conscious.
   • Human Medications Warning: NEVER give human painkillers like Paracetamol, Crocin, Ibuprofen, or Aspirin—they are fatal and cause acute liver/kidney failure in dogs.
   • Fractures / Spine Injury: Move the dog only on a flat, rigid board or taut blanket stretcher. Avoid bending the spine.
   • Respiratory Distress: Ensure airway is clear of vomit, blood, or tongue obstruction. Position head slightly elevated.

3. Broadcast a Community SOS:
   • Use the red 'REGISTER COMPLAINT / SOS' button on StreetPaw AI immediately. Our dispatch radar alerts volunteer rescuers and emergency NGO night ambulances across your city grid.

DOG BITE EMERGENCY PROTOCOL WHEN NO HOSPITALS ARE NEARBY:

1. Immediate Mechanical Flushing (Most Critical Step):
   • Flush the bite wound under high-pressure running tap water with ordinary alkaline bathing soap or detergent for a FULL 15 MINUTES.
   • Scientific Fact: Rabies virus has a lipid envelope that soap and running water dismantle, washing away over 90% of the viral load at the entry site before it penetrates nerves.

2. Chemical Disinfection:
   • After thorough washing, apply Povidone-Iodine (Betadine 5-10%), surgical spirit, or chlorhexidine generously into and around the wound.
   • If Betadine is unavailable, apply clean pure Dettol/Savlon solution or 70% alcohol.

3. Critical Do-NOTs (Avoid Home Remedy Mistakes):
   • NEVER apply turmeric powder, chili powder, mud, lime (chuna), coffee, or plant leaves onto the bite.
   • NEVER bandage or stitch the bite wound tightly. Rabies is an anaerobic virus; closing the wound deprives it of oxygen and drives the virus into nerves. Leave it open to breathe or cover very loosely with sterile gauze.

4. Control Active Bleeding:
   • If the bite caused heavy vascular bleeding, apply gentle direct pressure with clean gauze, but do not tie tight tourniquets.

5. Plan Immediate Transit (24 to 48 Hour Window):
   • Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (Anti-Rabies Vaccine - ARV) must be administered as early as possible (Day 0). You have a 24-48 hour window before the virus travels along peripheral nerves.
   • Arrange transport to the nearest government primary health center (PHC), community health center (CHC), or district hospital where ARV is free.
   • If it is a Category III bite (deep punctures, broken skin, or blood drawn), Rabies Immunoglobulin (RIG) is required alongside ARV.

6. Observe the Dog (If Feasible and Safe):
   • If the dog is a neighborhood stray or pet, observe it from a safe distance for 10-14 days. If it remains alive and healthy after 10 days, the risk of rabies transmission during that bite is virtually zero (though complete your ARV doses regardless).

HOW TO KNOW IF A DOG HAS RABIES (CLINICAL SYMPTOMS & OBSERVATION):

Rabies affects the central nervous system and typically presents in two distinct clinical forms:

1. Furious Rabies (Excitatory Phase — ~70% of cases):
   • Unprovoked Extreme Aggression: Snapping, lunging, and biting imaginary objects, walls, or any moving entity without warning.
   • Salivation & Inability to Swallow: Excessive thick, frothy ropy saliva dripping from the mouth due to paralysis of pharyngeal and throat muscles.
   • Hypersensitivity: Exaggerated agitation triggered by normal sounds, lights, or movement.
   • Altered Vocalization: A characteristic hoarse, raspy, strained bark or pitch change due to laryngeal paralysis.
   • Pica: Bizarre urge to chew or ingest non-food objects (rocks, plastic, stones, wood).

2. Dumb or Paralytic Rabies (~30% of cases):
   • 'Dropped Jaw' Sign: The lower jaw hangs limp, mouth stays open, and the dog cannot close it or swallow food/water.
   • Progressive Paralysis: Weakness starting in the hind legs, uncoordinated stumbling, ataxia, and eventual full-body recumbency.
   • Lethargy & Hiding: Withdrawn behavior, seeking dark quiet corners, non-responsive to familiar voices.

3. The 10-Day Quarantine Rule (Gold Standard Diagnostic):
   • Once clinical symptoms of rabies appear in a dog, the virus is in its final encephalitic stage and shedding in saliva.
   • A dog shedding rabies in its saliva will ALWAYS deteriorate rapidly and succumb within 7 to 10 days of symptom onset.
   • If the dog is alive, eating, and healthy 10 days after a bite, it DID NOT transmit rabies at the time of the bite.

4. What to Do If You Suspect Rabies:
   • NEVER attempt to touch, restrain, or feed the animal.
   • Alert BBMP / Municipal Animal Husbandry & local rescue squads immediately using the 'REGISTER COMPLAINT / SOS' button on StreetPaw AI so a specialized rabies catching team can safely isolate the animal under humane quarantine.
